q: You update a text variable and immediately try to extract the innerText value of its DOM node on the next line, but receive old content. How do you resolve this?
options: Trigger an internal component update manually
Wrap your DOM inspection code in nextTick
Convert your state structure to reactive proxies
Change the lifecycle implementation to onUpdated
explain: The framework batches reactive updates asynchronously. Calling nextTick returns a promise that resolves immediately after the microtask queue finishes flushing accumulated DOM adjustments.

q: You are writing automated unit tests for an input form component using script setup. How do you expose a local validation method to your wrapper test tool?
options: Export the method from a secondary script tag
Declare the method using the defineExpose macro
Attach your method directly onto instance proxies
Pass the validation handler using defined emits
explain: Components using script setup are fully closed by default. You must invoke the defineExpose compiler macro to explicitly declare which state or properties are accessible from outside.

q: You are building an online map component that receives an expensive dataset object as a prop which should never have its internal parameters observed. What should you do?
options: Store your dataset inside a shallowRef variable
Wrap the incoming data with standard reactive
Observe mutations using deep watch structures
Extract object values using the toRaw helper
explain: A shallowRef observes changes restricted to its base value property pointer. Properties hidden inside deep sub-objects avoid heavy recursive reactivity proxy wrapping.

q: You need to invoke an asynchronous data search method instantly when a search field component renders, and also on all subsequent user keystrokes. Which setup is ideal?
options: Run your fetch inside standard onBeforeMount hooks
Configure a watch callback with immediate true
Structure your call inside computed getter blocks
Execute the query method inside nextTick loops
explain: Setting the immediate option to true instructs a watcher to fire its callback immediately upon creation, satisfying initial data fetching and subsequent update tracking simultaneously.

q: You have a deep state object containing multiple form steps and need to trigger a parent validation rule when any nested child parameter shifts. How do you observe this?
options: Re-evaluate data using active watchSyncEffect utilities
Configure your watch property with deep true
Bind all properties using separate multi-model components
Map individual data elements using unref macros
explain: Standard watchers skip nested object mutations for efficiency. Enforcing the deep option instructs the engine to recursively traverse all internal sub-properties to register reactive tracking loops.

q: You are building an overlay modal component that is nested deep inside a multi-layered layouts grid but must be rendered directly under the document body element. What resolves this?
options: Portal the content using custom styles definitions
Wrap the target block inside Teleport tags
Mount an external component instance using refs
Extract the layout tree via nextTick commands
explain: The Teleport component relocates its nested slot nodes to a target DOM destination container while perfectly maintaining logical connectivity and component lifecycle hooks.

q: You want to abstract and export an isolated browser geolocation tracker feature to share across multiple dashboard components. Which architectural pattern should you use?
options: Mixins structures
Composables functions
Plugins declarations
Provide abstractions
explain: Composables harness the Composition API to package and export stateful business logic. They provide clean code reuse without the naming clashes and scope confusion of legacy mixins.

q: You are designing a custom text component and need to modify the input text to uppercase before syncing it back to the parent data state. How do you handle this?
options: Transform properties inside a watchSyncEffect block
Create a custom modifier on defineModel variables
Overwrite properties inside onBeforeUpdate lifecycle hooks
Reconstruct inputs using standard defineEmits tracking array
explain: The defineModel macro lets you access custom v-model modifiers. It reads the parent flags and processes updates to filter, format, or transform string states smoothly.

q: You are creating a flexible custom card element that must capture class names and placeholder parameters from parents without registering them as official props. Where do they go?
options: They are automatically mapped onto the $attrs reference
They are injected downstream via specific slots references
They are collected inside the global customRef array
They are dropped completely unless mapped via defineProps
explain: Attributes omitted from explicit prop validation lists are grouped into the component fallthrough attributes object. These are accessed in templates via the $attrs property.

q: You need to manipulate an HTML5 video canvas node directly to play and pause media clips from your setup function. How do you fetch its reference?
options: Query the DOM using browser querySelector commands
Declare a template ref matching the ref string
Extract elements via the customRef utility method
Bind an inline custom event handler onUpdate
explain: Declaring a reactive variable whose name matches the template element ref attribute populates it with the underlying native DOM node instance after layout mounting finishes.

q: You are migrating a component to script setup and want to override its development display name and turn off default attribute inheritance. Which macro handles this?
options: defineModel
defineOptions
defineProps
defineExpose
explain: The defineOptions macro lets you declare traditional component options like name and inheritAttrs directly inside script setup blocks without using auxiliary script tags.

q: You have an asynchronous dashboard layout containing slow third-party user graphs that takes seconds to initialize. What element helps manage the fallback layout UI?
explain: The Suspense built-in element coordinates async dependencies down its component tree. It displays a #fallback slot template while nested components resolve their async setups.

q: You are refactoring an app view containing an input wizard where users lose entered text when jumping back and forth across separate step tabs. What solves this?
options: Wrap the dynamic component inside KeepAlive tags
Isolate components using distinct watchPostEffect loops
Inject states using alternative shallowReactive setups
Enforce unique random key attributes on templates
explain: The KeepAlive component preserves inactive element states within an memory cache. It bypasses destruction lifecycles to re-insert components with their data states intact.

q: You are implementing type annotations for an explicit emit dictionary using modern TypeScript features in a script setup component. Which approach is valid?
options: Pass functional interface properties directly into defineEmits
Use labeled tuple syntax within defineEmits generic arguments
Export method type definitions via defineOptions macros
Annotate returned references using standard computed types
explain: Modern Vue type checking processes generic arguments in defineEmits using labeled tuples. This models signature properties directly for enhanced IDE auto-completion.

q: You want to create a reusable input component that supports dual bindings for both a primary text entry string and an secondary validation boolean. How do you implement this?
options: Declare multiple named defineModel properties inside setup
Combine properties inside a single watchSyncEffect hook
Expose parameters via the default defineExpose macro
Inject variables downstream using global provide states
explain: You can declare multiple custom v-model bindings on one component by assigning distinct string names as arguments inside your defineModel macro calls.

q: You are maintaining a shared form state inside a core parent shell but want to prevent child elements from accidentally changing values via inject slots. How do you protect it?
options: Provide the value wrapped inside the readonly helper
Isolate parameters using a local shallowReactive proxy
Cast variables using the raw toValue extractor
Enforce execution through the watchSyncEffect loop
explain: The readonly function maps a deep non-reactive proxy barrier over state objects. Any modification attempts by child targets fail with clear console warning logs.

q: You want to develop an enterprise localization feature that injects translation helpers globally across all components in your application. What mechanism should you write?
options: A custom composable function
A custom Vue plugin with an install method
An asynchronous provide config provider
A global navigation router guard
explain: Vue plugins use an install method to configure app instances. They can register global directives, update properties, or provide global variables.

q: You need to access style properties inside a scoped CSS block using a reactive numeric variable called cardHeight computed in setup. Which tool implements this?
options: The CSS Modules layout mixin
The native CSS v-bind functional property
The global :global modifier expression
The scoped data-v data attribute selector
explain: The v-bind syntax in style tags maps dynamic javascript variables to CSS custom variables, keeping component styles reactive without writing inline style bindings.

q: You are writing a composable helper and want it to accept an argument that could be a plain string, a reactive ref, or a dynamic getter function. Which utility unwraps it safely?
options: unref
toValue
isRef
toRaw
explain: The toValue utility normalized flexible inputs. It unwraps standard ref wrappers and executes getter functions to safely return the resolved raw value.

q: You want to monitor store mutations globally to sync them with browser localStorage fields on every mutation step. Which Pinia utility should you track?
options: store.$onAction
store.$subscribe
store.$patch
store.$reset
explain: The store.$subscribe method attaches a listener callback to state changes. It tracks all updates and identifies patch types for easy persistence.

q: You are setting up multi-step forms using routing structures and want to store distinct access permissions configuration right on your route definitions. Where should this live?
options: Inside the query string parameters template
Inside the route custom meta fields dictionary
Inside the global app configuration handler
Inside separate component-level provide definitions
explain: Route meta configurations attach arbitrary data blocks to paths. This metadata can be read inside navigation guards to implement route access validation safely.

q: You notice that navigating between identical profile paths like /user/1 and /user/2 skips unmounting hooks, keeping your data stale on screen. How do you intercept this parameter shift?
options: Re-trigger lifecycle execution with onUpdated hooks
Watch the route params object for changes
Re-route applications using alternative router.replace
Isolate components using explicit defineOptions configuration
explain: Vue Router reuses mounted component structures when navigating identical patterns for speed. Watching the route.params dictionary allows you to re-fetch data on parameter updates.

q: You want to override standard navigation flow to verify authentication cookies before a browser starts rendering a target page. Which mechanism do you write?
options: An onServerPrefetch tracking block
A global router beforeEach navigation guard
An app config error handling callback
A reactive watchSyncEffect state hook
explain: The router.beforeEach guard intercepts navigation pipelines sequentially. It pauses routing steps to evaluate validation rules before passing execution forward.

q: You are style-customizing an imported third-party calendar item and need your scoped style block to match an internal child selector class named calendar-day. What do you use?
options: The :global() helper function element
The :deep() selector modifier function
The :slotted() style definition wrapper
The module style custom hash attribute
explain: The :deep() functional pseudo-selector forces compiled scoped rules to bypass the current data attribute scope restriction, targeting child layout nodes safely.

q: You are designing an expansive dropdown selection item that opens with custom animations. What lifecycle hook signals a child component inside KeepAlive is toggled back into view?
options: onMounted
onActivated
onUpdated
onBeforeMount
explain: Components preserved within KeepAlive bypass normal mounting cycles on return visits. They trigger the specialized onActivated lifecycle hook instead when toggled into active layout views.
